title: One hard prerequisite per lesson
statement: Let a lesson depend on at most one hard prerequisite, and treat needing more as a sign the lesson is oversized and should be split, not given more gates.
detail: Sequencing briefs for a Grade 3 and a Grade 6 reading course cap hard prerequisites at one per lesson. In the Grade 3 brief a hard prerequisite is an earlier lesson in the unit without which the lesson's task breaks, and each lesson teaches exactly one new operation and depends on what at most one earlier lesson added. Exceeding the cap is read as an oversized lesson, not as a need for more gating; the Grade 6 brief ties the cap to a test of whether the earlier knowledge can be retrieved at the point of use. It is a declared rule for lightly gated reading courses; no outcome was measured.

evidence.quote: **Max hard prereqs per lesson: 1.** Each dose teaches exactly one new operation and depends on at most one prior within-unit column. Exceeding this signals an oversized lesson, not a gating need.
**Max hard prereqs per lesson: 1** (point-of-use retrievability test — the curriculum-graph guidance). Exceeding it signals an oversized KC, not more gating.
